subject: Gaza Ceasefire Resolution
overview: The Medford City Council approved a resolution calling for an enduring bilateral ceasefire in Israel and Gaza following extensive public comment. The council also called the March 2024 presidential primary election, resolved to support plant medicine decriminalization upon reconsideration, and addressed several local commercial, facilities, and neighborhood issues.

items.title: Ceremonial resolutions and committee reports
items.summary: The council approved resolutions celebrating Black History Month, honoring Patrick O'Brien, and sending condolences to the families of Bruno 'Bruni' Bonacorsi and Elizabeth 'Betsy' Schwerer, followed by approval of prior minutes and multiple committee reports.

items.title: Public participation on Jingle Bell Festival
items.summary: Residents and organizers spoke in support of the annual Jingle Bell Festival at City Hall and the Community Family adult day health center, receiving council assurances that there are no plans to cancel or displace the event.

items.title: Call for presidential preferential primary
items.summary: Approved the call and polling locations for the March 5, 2024 presidential primary election, retaining the Walkling Court location, and placed the 2024 election calendar on file.

items.title: Gaza ceasefire resolution
items.summary: Adopted an amended resolution supporting an enduring bilateral ceasefire in Israel and Gaza, the release of hostages and detainees, and humanitarian aid delivery, following extensive testimony from residents with family ties to the region, local activists, and community members.

items.title: Diversity, equity, and inclusion trainings
items.summary: Referred a proposal to hold biannual DEI refreshers with the Director of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion to the Resident Services and Public Engagement Committee, with an amendment to explore extending the trainings to city boards and commissions.

items.title: Warming and cooling center exploration
items.summary: Referred a resolution to the Public Health and Community Safety Committee to explore city spaces, operating costs, and partnerships to open an adult warming and cooling center by December 2024.

items.title: Resolution calling on US government to end Cuba embargo
items.summary: Approved a resolution urging the federal government to lift the embargo against Cuba and remove it from the state sponsors of terrorism list.

items.title: Commercial vacancy tax discussion
items.summary: Referred a proposal to study a commercial vacancy tax targeting indefinitely empty storefronts to the Administration and Finance Committee.

items.title: Transportation demand ordinance
items.summary: Referred a proposed transportation demand management ordinance to the Planning and Permitting Committee for coordination with the comprehensive zoning reform process.

items.title: BJ's Wholesale Club construction updates and neighborhood concerns
items.summary: Referred neighborhood vibration and infrastructure concerns from gas station pylon work to the Building Department for immediate response and abutters notification, while tabling the paper for future council review.

items.title: Zoning review and facilities management requests
items.summary: Referred the comprehensive zoning review project to Planning and Permitting to engage consultants, and referred a request for a municipal building inventory and repair cost assessment to Public Works and Facilities.

items.title: Reconsideration of plant medicine resolution
items.summary: Reconsidered paper 24-021 following an earlier vote to send it to committee, and approved the resolution supporting adult access and decriminalization of entheogenic plant medicine with an amendment requesting a response from the police chief.
